; SPIR-V
; Version: 1.0
; Generator: Google spiregg; 0
; Bound: 23
; Schema: 0
               OpCapability Shader
               OpCapability SampledBuffer
               OpCapability ImageBuffer
               OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450
               OpEntryPoint GLCompute %main "main" %gl_GlobalInvocationID
               OpExecutionMode %main LocalSize 1 1 1
          %3 = OpString "/app/example.hlsl"
               OpSource HLSL 600 %3 "//==========================================================================//
// #3726 -- \"Sema should not allow assignment to resource\" (open since 2021-04).
//
// The source is a compute-shader restating of the issue's pixel-shader repro, because
// Clang's DXIL backend cannot lower a pixel shader writing SV_Target. getResource()
// assigns the global resource r0 to an `out` resource parameter; main() passes the
// other global, x0, as that argument. The stage-accurate original is in the repo.
//
// What to look at, pane by pane:
//
//   dxc_1_6_2112 / dxc_trunk        Rejected -- but not by Sema. The error comes out
//       of the DXIL lowering pass DxilLowerCreateHandleForLib, roughly 150 passes
//       after code generation. It shows: the first line is a library-export message
//       on a compute shader with no library functions, naming a mangled global.
//       Add -fcgl (stop after front-end IR) and every DXC release from v1.4.1907 to
//       today exits 0 with an empty stderr, so nothing in the front end objects.
//
//   dxc_trunk -spirv                Exit 0, no diagnostic -- and the module binds x0,
//       the assignment's target, while r0, its source, does not appear at all. That
//       is the opposite resource from the one the DXIL path refuses to allow.
//
//   hlsl_clang_trunk                Exit 0, no diagnostic -- and its resource-binding
//       table names r0, not x0. The successor front end accepts the assignment and
//       gives it the copy semantics the DXIL path rejects.
//
// Three back ends, three answers, and no front end diagnoses anything. Whether Sema
// should reject this at all, and how narrowly, is a language-design question: declare
// x0 `static`, or declare it inside main() instead of at global scope, and DXC's DXIL
// path compiles the very same assignment cleanly today.
//==========================================================================//

// #3726 -- compute-shader restating of repro.hlsl, for the Compiler Explorer pane.
//
// Why it exists: Clang's DXIL backend cannot lower a pixel shader writing SV_Target
// (SKILL.md step 7), and the issue's repro is exactly that, so a Clang pane on
// repro.hlsl would be full of noise about the stage rather than about the issue.
// Compute is the stage all three compilers can answer on. Reduced to one RWBuffer
// because that is the resource type Clang's HLSL support is furthest along on --
// the construct under test is `out`-parameter assignment of a global resource, which
// is not specific to Texture2D.
//
// Verified before adoption: DXC reproduces the SAME back-end error on this file that
// it does on repro.hlsl, and -fcgl is equally silent on it (variant-cs-dxil-*.txt and
// variant-cs-fcgl-*.txt). repro.hlsl remains the stage-accurate local evidence.
RWBuffer<float4> r0;
RWBuffer<float4> x0;

void getResource(out RWBuffer<float4> a0)
{
    a0 = r0;
}

[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
void main(uint3 tid : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    getResource(x0);
    x0[tid.x] = 1;
}
"
               OpName %type_buffer_image "type.buffer.image"
               OpName %x0 "x0"
               OpName %main "main"
               OpDecorate %gl_GlobalInvocationID BuiltIn GlobalInvocationId
               OpDecorate %x0 DescriptorSet 0
               OpDecorate %x0 Binding 1
      %float = OpTypeFloat 32
    %float_1 = OpConstant %float 1
    %v4float = OpTypeVector %float 4
          %9 = OpConstantComposite %v4float %float_1 %float_1 %float_1 %float_1
        %int = OpTypeInt 32 1
      %int_0 = OpConstant %int 0
%type_buffer_image = OpTypeImage %float Buffer 2 0 0 2 Rgba32f

       %uint = OpTypeInt 32 0
     %v3uint = OpTypeVector %uint 3
